<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import jack "fire:backend/jack"
```

JACK driver: the JACK server is the device. We register one JACK port per
channel; JACK's realtime thread calls us once per period. libjack is loaded
at run time (create returns .Unsupported without it). See /design/backend/.

## Types

### Options

```odin
Options :: struct {
	client_name: string,
	server_name: string,
	auto_connect: bool,
}
```

Settings for create. Start from default_options.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `client_name` | "" = "Fire Engine" |
| `server_name` | "" = the default server |
| `auto_connect` | Connect our ports to the physical ports (output k → playback k, capture k → input k) at start. Off for apps that route themselves. |

## Procedures

### default_options

```odin
default_options :: proc() -> Options
```

Defaults: client "Fire Engine" on the default server, auto_connect on.

### create

```odin
create :: proc(opts: Options = Options{auto_connect = true}, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (^backend.Driver, core.Error)
```

Makes a JACK driver. Returns .Unsupported if libjack cannot be loaded; a
missing server shows up later (enumerate lists no devices, open fails).
Free with backend.driver_destroy. Control thread.

### port_name

```odin
port_name :: proc(d: ^backend.Driver, output: bool, channel: int) -> string
```

The full JACK name ("client:port") of our port for a channel, for routing.

### connect

```odin
connect :: proc(d: ^backend.Driver, source: string, destination: string) -> core.Error
```

Connects two JACK ports by full name (ours or anyone's). While running.
